descriptions.archival_availability: National or archive-level survival and access; it is not a count of people represented in this project.
descriptions.index_vs_original: An index or transcript is a finding aid. Treat an original, certified copy, or digitised image as separate evidence and record which was inspected.
descriptions.absence: A missing search result cannot establish that an event or person did not exist; coverage, jurisdiction, spelling, loss and indexing must be checked first.
descriptions.local_counts: Any row totals in project datasets are local collection counts and must not be presented as archival survival totals.

jurisdictions.Ireland: Coverage and repository custody differ between all-island records and the separate jurisdictions after partition in 1922; some will-calendar series divide earlier.
jurisdictions.Scotland: National Records of Scotland (NRS) and ScotlandsPeople provide the principal national record access.
jurisdictions.England: England and Wales civil registration and census guidance is administered through the GRO and The National Archives.
jurisdictions.United States: The National Archives holds federal census records; survival varies by census year.
jurisdictions.Canada: Use Library and Archives Canada census and civil-registration guidance; this file makes no completeness claim beyond verified collections below.
jurisdictions.Australia: Use the relevant state or territory archive/registrar; this file makes no national completeness claim.
jurisdictions.New Zealand: Use Archives New Zealand and the Registrar-General; this file makes no national completeness claim.

census/ireland/1821-1851.title: Irish census survivals and substitutes, 1821–1851
paragraphs: Most 1821, 1831, 1841 and 1851 returns were destroyed in the 1922 fire. Surviving original fragments include Antrim 1851; Belfast one ward 1851; Dublin city heads-of-household index 1851; Fermanagh 1821/1841/1851; Cavan 1821/1841; Cork 1841; Galway 1821; Offaly 1821; Meath 1821; Waterford 1841; and Londonderry/Derry 1831 with 1834 revisions.

The Derry 1831 material includes names of householders and counts by religion and sex, with 1834 revisions. It is not a person-by-person list of every household member. Search transcripts are finding aids; verify the scanned return and record omissions.

census/ireland/1861-1891.title: Irish census losses, 1861–1891
paragraphs: No individual household returns survive for 1861, 1871, 1881 or 1891: 1861/1871 were destroyed after analysis and 1881/1891 were pulped during the First World War.

census/ireland/1901-1911.title: Irish census household returns, 1901 and 1911
paragraphs: These are the only complete surviving pre-Independence Irish census records; original household returns survive across all 32 counties and are searchable with images. A project sample remains a local count, not a national count.

census/ireland/1926.title: Irish Free State census, 1926
paragraphs: The 1926 Irish Free State census is now available through the National Archives of Ireland. It covers the Free State, not all 32 counties. The 1901/1911 search form is separate from the 1926 service; follow the official 1926 link. This project has not yet collected references from that release.

census/scotland/1841-1921.title: Scottish census records
paragraphs: The open Scottish census series runs from 1841 to 1921 at ten-year intervals. The available images are enumerators’ transcript books made from household schedules; the original household schedules were destroyed. Some 1841 books are missing.

civil/ireland/bmd.title: Irish civil births, marriages and deaths
paragraphs: Civil indexes and images online cover births 1864–1925; marriages 1845–1950 (non-Roman Catholic from 1845, Roman Catholic from 1864); deaths generally 1871–1975, with earlier death material being added or patchy. An index hit is not itself an inspected register image.

civil/scotland/statutory.title: Scottish statutory BMD registers
paragraphs: Compulsory civil registration began in 1855. Statutory births, deaths and marriages are index-linked digital images through ScotlandsPeople, with online privacy cutoffs; certificates or official extracts are distinct from indexes.

church/scotland/opr.title: Scottish Old Parish Registers
paragraphs: OPRs cover 1553–1854 and contain Church of Scotland baptisms/births, banns/marriages and deaths/burials. Survival and registration are uneven; some parishes begin late or have no surviving records.

civil/england-wales/bmd.title: England and Wales civil registration
paragraphs: The GRO holds registered births, marriages and deaths from 1 July 1837. Its public index lists basic details; certificates, PDFs and online images are separate access products. Parish registers are needed for earlier research.

census/england-wales/1841-1921.title: England and Wales census records
paragraphs: The National Archives guides access to censuses 1841–1921 through official partners and archive holdings. The 1931 census was destroyed by fire in 1942; no 1941 census was taken.

probate/ireland/1858-1922.title: Irish probate and testamentary records
paragraphs: Before 1857 the Church of Ireland held testamentary jurisdiction; from 1858 civil probate registries issued grants. Calendars are finding aids and an entry does not prove the underlying will survives; the 1922 fire destroyed many originals.

land/ireland/tithe-1823-1837.title: Irish Tithe Applotment Books
paragraphs: Compiled 1823–1837, generally listing occupiers of productive/tithable agricultural holdings, acreage/value and tithe. They usually identify occupiers rather than all household members and do not systematically cover urban land.

land/ireland/griffiths-1847-1864.title: Irish Primary Valuation (Griffith’s Valuation)
paragraphs: Published 1847–1864, this property valuation lists occupiers, lessors and property amount/value. It is an occupancy/property source and should not be treated as a household census.

census/united-states/1890.title: United States 1890 census
paragraphs: Most population schedules were destroyed in the 1921 Commerce Department fire. Fragments survive for parts of 10 states and Washington, DC, plus separate Union veterans/widows schedules; fragments cannot support national absence claims.
